p: on the verse "and he lay down in that place" (Bereishis 28:11):
that he was hidden away in the house of Ever

and to the darkness of the generations;

rich.text: — וישכב במקום ההוא, רבי יהודה ורבי נחמיה, רבי יהודה אמר כאן שכב אבל כל ארבע עשרה שנה שהיה טמון בבית עבר לא שכב, ורבי נחמיה אמר כאן שכב אבל כל עשרים שנה שעמד בביתו של לבן לא שכב, ומה היה אומר … רבי שמואל בר נחמן אמר כל ספר תהלים היה אומר, מה טעם ואתה קדוש יושב תהלות ישראל, ישראל סבא. (on “these twenty years”), and in Midrash Tehillim 124:1.

h: Three Holy Traits and Their Opposites

p: Now, just as the three traits
are the root of eternal life,
so too, one corresponding to the other,
which "remove a person from the world" (Avot 4:21).
of love — the Chesed of holiness.
This is Yishmael, the dross of Avraham,
as written in the holy Zohar.
is the opposite of the Gevurah of holiness,
and it is the dross of Yitzchak:
whose bed was complete [with no dross].
Nevertheless, there is a refinement [of good]
Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
was lowly in his own eyes,
"I am too small for all the kindnesses" (Bereishis 32:11);
and he is the root of the Torah of truth,
and go to a low place, like water
And specifically about them it is said,
Now Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
when he went into exile to the house of Lavan,
and the root of the opposing side,
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
About this Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said
that is, to rectify the flaw of desire.
As in the matter of what is said
descending from the Court of Israel
corresponding to the fifteen Songs of Ascents
when they conduct themselves in holiness,
the yud in ish (man) and the heh in ishah (woman)
of this world and of the World to Come.
to the completeness of the World to Come,
and that is in the man,
which is "a tree of life to those who grasp it" (Mishlei 3:18).
to the completeness of the life of this world,
which is not through Torah study [itself]
"by bringing their sons to the synagogue [to learn]," etc.

rich.text: (Balak) — Rav Tzadok gives no address. The closest Zohar passage found: when the Torah is offered to the angel of the right-hand “arm” (Yishmael's line) and he hears “You shall not commit adultery,” he cries: ווי אי ירותא דא יחסין לי קודשא בריך הוא … דהא ברכתא דמיא נטילנא, ברכתא דנוני ימא, דכתיב פרו ורבו … וכתיב והפריתי אותו והרביתי אותו … וכתיב והוא יהיה פרא אדם. His whole dominion is the “blessing of water,” the fruitfulness promised to Yishmael, which adultery-free Torah would take from him. This fits both Rav Tzadok's claim here and his linking of Yishmael's desire with the “arrogant waters” in ¶3; but since he does not cite a page, the identification is not certain.

h: David, the Deep, and the Fifteen Ascents

p: Now, it is related in the Gemara
When David dug [the foundations of the altar],
and sought to flood the world, etc.
He said: the higher it rises,
the more the world is moistened.
He recited the fifteen [Songs of] Ascents
and raised it fifteen thousand cubits, etc.
The matter is according to what is known
that the evil inclination of desire
for it will be whitened in the Future to Come;
for the evil inclination is needed
for the joy of Torah study.
About this our Sages, of blessed memory, said
drag him to the study hall."
That is, the evil inclination of desire,
so that the desire and the longing will be
It is known that water is
and of longing for and love of the Torah.
and "the waters of the great deep,"
which is the root of the idolatrous nations,
"like the roaring of the seas they roar" (Yeshayahu 17:12).
וְעַל יְדֵי הַחֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שִׁיר הַמַּעֲלוֹת
And through the fifteen Songs of Ascents
that King David, peace be upon him, recited,
he raised the waters of the deep
that is, to the aspect of living waters
As is alluded to in the holy Zohar
all the wellsprings of the great deep" (Bereishis 7:11):
the waters of the deep will be elevated
that the fifteen Songs of Ascents
in order to rectify the flaw of desire
and to raise it to holiness.
"Were it not for Hashem who was with us,
"Then would have passed over our soul
And only Israel the Elder raised them up,
עַל יְדֵי חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שִׁיר הַמַּעֲלוֹת
through the fifteen Songs of Ascents,

rich.text: — הכי אתמר, בשעה שכרה דוד שיתין קפא תהומא ובעא למשטפא עלמא; continued on

h: Three Camps, Three Impurities, Three Flaws

p: about sending out from three camps,
the zav, the metzora, and one impure through a corpse —
comes for the flaw of evil speech,
which stems from envy and anger;
and that is the trait of Esav,
which has no rectification at all,
even in the Future to Come,
"And there shall be no survivor," etc. (Ovadyah 1:18).
"the anger of the Sages, which is good," etc.,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, קפב עַמּוּד ב)
that is only in this world,
כָּל זְמַן שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק קַיָּם
as long as the seed of Amalek exists;
But in the Future to Come,
when the seed of Amalek will perish,
nothing of this will remain at all,
and it will have no rectification whatsoever.
Therefore the metzora is sent out
even from the camp of Israel,
no elevation in holiness at all.
This is not so of the zav,
who corresponds to the flaw of desire:
he is not sent out of the camp of Israel,
because [desire] has an elevation in holiness,
he is sent out only from the Levite camp,
for he has no cleaving to holiness;
from what is said, "and they shall join you" (Bamidbar 18:2).
And one impure through the dead is alluded to
as corresponding to the flaw of honor and self-elevation.
the essence of the breaking and the death
as it says, "Hashem reigns; He is clothed in majesty" (Tehillim 93:1).
For He needed, as it were,
for the sake of the Kingdom of Heaven;
the aspect of "the primordial kings who died,"
שֶׁכָּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ
that any person who has arrogance
is as though he worships idols.
of ruling over the whole world,
he said, "I will ascend above the heights of the clouds;
I will be like the Most High" (Yeshayahu 14:14).

p: And this too was the intent
of King David, peace be upon him,
in asking that it be considered —
like engaging in Nega'im and Ohalot:
that is, that it be possible
which are severe and weighty in this world.
the statement of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman
that the entire Book of Tehillim
Yaakov would say in Lavan's house.
For certainly he labored there to rectify
those of envy and honor too,
just like the flaw of desire
according to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi;
all three flaws for all generations,
the root of life in holiness,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִשְׁרָשׁ עַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּנוּ
so that thereby there be rooted in us
the three traits of the holy Avos.
For in the meal of the Field of Apples (Chakal Tapuchin),
the flaw of desire is rectified;
for "he dwelt in the land of the Negev" (Bereishis 24:62),
from all the desires of the world.
And in the meal of Atika Kadisha,
the flaw of anger and envy is rectified;
for the trait of Avraham Avinu
was that he was clean and purified
of the aspect of Gevurot entirely.
And in the third meal, that of Ze'ir Anpin,
the flaw of self-elevation is rectified.
